title: Home Inspector Local Services Ads: 7 Problems Inspectors Report and How to Fix Them
html:
Home inspector Local Services Ads usually stop producing leads for one of five reasons: a recent service area change, a duplicate or unlinked account, a paused or suspended Google Business Profile, slow review growth, or poor lead handling in the dashboard. Fix the account setup first, keep reviews coming every week, mark booked jobs, and rate every lead. Raising the budget rarely helps when you are already spending well under your cap.

Home inspector Local Services Ads can be the cheapest source of booked inspections in your market, or a line item that quietly stops working. Inspectors who post about their accounts in local search communities describe the same pattern: steady leads for months, then a sharp drop with no warning and no clear answer from support. This guide covers the seven problems that come up most often and what to do about each one. Inspectors should also read the pay-per-lead goals terms that advertisers report seeing in Google Ads.

Is Local Services Ads worth it for home inspectors?

Yes, for most home inspectors Local Services Ads are worth running, because "home inspector" is a supported category and you pay per lead instead of per click. Google lists home inspectors among the service categories where Local Services Ads are available, and the ads sit above regular search ads for searches like "home inspector near me.". Plumbers face a similar list in 6 plumber LSA problems.

The catch is that Local Services Ads give you very few controls. You cannot write ad copy or bid on keywords. Your placement depends mostly on your reviews, your responsiveness, your service area, and how Google judges your account's history. That is why the problems below are mostly about account health, not ad strategy.

Should home inspectors manage Local Services Ads themselves or hire help?

You can run Local Services Ads yourself if you have time each week for lead rating, review requests, and account checks. Hire help when leads drop and you cannot find the cause, or when you run several territories. Contractors in community threads are blunt about it: the controls look simple, but diagnosing a drop takes experience with how account changes, profile links, and service areas interact.

If you hire, ask how the manager handles lead rating, profile link checks, and service area changes, and ask to see how they report cost per booked inspection. You can also pair Local Services Ads with Meta Ads for home inspectors to stay in front of agents and buyers between searches.

Can home inspectors run Google Local Services Ads?

Yes. Home inspector is one of the service categories where Google offers Local Services Ads. You must pass Google's business screening first, which includes license and background checks that vary by state and typically take two to four weeks. After approval, you pay per lead instead of per click.

How long does it take Local Services Ads to recover after a change?

Owners in local search communities report recovery in about two to three weeks after reversing a service area change. That timeline comes from owner experience, not from Google. Make one change at a time, log the date of each change, and compare impressions and leads against the prior four weeks.
